title: Pick One Per Column, Min Range
statement:
You are given a matrix `A` with `N` rows and `M` columns of positive integers. You start in any row of the first column and must reach the last column. From a cell in column `j` you may jump to **any** row of column `j + 1`. In other words, you pick exactly one element from every column, and the rows you pick in different columns are completely independent.

If the elements you picked are `P1, P2, ..., PM` (one from each column, in order), the **cost** of the path is `max(P1, ..., PM) - min(P1, ..., PM)`.

Print the minimum possible cost.

**Follow-up:** A variant of this question, reported in another interview, picks one element from each row (rows may have different lengths) and asks you to print the chosen elements themselves, in sorted order, for a choice with the smallest max-minus-min.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `N` and `M`.
Each of the next `N` lines contains `M` integers: the rows of the matrix.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum possible cost.

examples.explanation: Pick the `1` from column 1 (row 0), the `1` from column 2 (row 2) and the `1` from column 3 (row 2). All chosen values are equal, so the cost is 1 - 1 = 0.
Column 1 offers {1, 2}, column 2 offers {10, 11}, column 3 offers {20, 30}. The best choice is 2, 11, 20 with range 18; choosing 1, 10, 20 gives 19.
With a single row every column has just one choice, so the picked values are 5, 1, 9, 3 and the cost is 9 - 1 = 8.

hints: Fix a window of values [lo, hi]. The choice is feasible exactly when every column has at least one element inside the window.
Sort all N·M cells by value, remembering each cell's column. Now the question becomes: find the shortest value window over this sorted list that contains cells from all M columns.

Use two pointers with a per-column counter and a count of columns currently covered. Extend the right end until every column is covered, then shrink the left end while it stays covered, recording max - min each time.
